beats.care: Flying abroad this winter? Fewer slots could mean fewer flight options. Check your booking and keep Navi Mumbai airport in mind.
beats.what: MIAL plans to rebuild Terminal 1B's northern part from January 2027 and shift those passengers to T2, cutting international departure slots by 33%.
beats.why: About 5 million yearly passengers would be affected. Airlines say their winter schedules were already approved in June.

cards.body: No final number of flights or start date has been fixed yet.
cards.caption: Proposed cut in international departure slots

cards.body: Mumbai's airline operators committee wrote on Oct 2 that the proposal was "not accepted". Talks were set for Oct 13.
The airport is offering airlines a 100% landing-fee discount on new international flights from Navi Mumbai, about 36 km away.

cards.q: Would you fly abroad from Navi Mumbai?

opts: To rebuild part of the old Terminal 1
cards.q: Why does Mumbai airport want to cut slots?
cards.why: MIAL wants to rebuild Terminal 1B from January 2027 and shift passengers to Terminal 2.

hook: Why does Mumbai airport want *fewer international flights*?

learn.t: Mumbai's Terminal 1 building is about 60 years old; its rebuilt section should handle 20 million passengers a year.

sources.name: Business Standard (Reuters)
sources.title: Why Mumbai airport and airlines are at odds over proposed flight cuts

tldr: Mumbai airport wants to cut international departure slots by a third to rebuild part of Terminal 1, but airlines have pushed back.
watch: Cuts once planned from October 25 were deferred by a few weeks; Terminal 1B rebuild starts January 2027.
